patients.summary: Administrative assistant who joined the practice healthy in 2019. Heavy periods from a submucosal fibroid (resected 2022) led to iron deficiency anemia and then restless legs; pulmonary arterial hypertension was diagnosed by an outside pulmonology group in 2024 and treated with tadalafil. Last seen January 2026 for a wellness visit with ongoing fatigue.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller wants to transfer her primary care here; says the membership model appeals to her because she can never get a same-week appointment where she is now. Healthy, no regular meds per caller. Commercial PPO card info taken. New patient physical scheduled 6/11 at 8:40. Records release form emailed for her prior office.

reports.text: Specimen: cervical, liquid-based. Adequacy: satisfactory for evaluation; transformation zone component present. Interpretation: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV: not detected.

documents.title: New Patient Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
32-year-old woman establishing care. Transferring from another primary care office for easier access; she has had no ongoing problems there.

HISTORY: Generally well. No chronic illnesses. No hospitalizations. Takes no prescription or OTC medicines regularly.
OB/GYN: G1P1, one uncomplicated vaginal delivery. Menses monthly and manageable, about 5 days. Last Pap at prior office, normal per patient; records requested.
Surgical: none apart from the delivery.
Allergies: none to medications.
Family: mother has fibroids and restless legs. A maternal aunt has pulmonary arterial hypertension. No other heart, lung or blood disorders she knows of.
Social: administrative assistant, desk work. Never smoked. Does not drink. No drug use.

ROS: negative across systems; no fatigue, dyspnea, bleeding problems.

EXAM: Pleasant, well appearing. Vitals per flowsheet. HEENT unremarkable. Thyroid not enlarged. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no masses. Extremities warm, no swelling. Skin clear. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix appears healthy, uterus normal size and nontender, no adnexal fullness. Pap with HPV obtained.

ASSESSMENT/PLAN:
1. Adult preventive care. Tdap given today (last tetanus unknown). CBC, CMP, lipids, TSH. One-time HIV and hepatitis C screening, she agrees. PHQ-2 negative.
2. Cervical screening: co-test sent; if negative, next in 5 years.
3. Family history noted; nothing to act on now.
Follow up yearly or as needed. She has the portal and knows she can text.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Tamika, your blood count, chemistry panel, thyroid and cholesterol all look healthy. HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. The Pap result usually takes a few more days; I'll message you when it posts.

documents.title: Pap result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Pap smear was normal and the HPV test was negative. You won't need another until 2024.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Fourteen pages faxed from her previous primary care office, covering 2014 to 2019. Contents: yearly physicals with normal exams; Pap 2016 negative; tetanus status not documented; no chronic problems; no prescriptions on file; allergies listed as none. Routed to PCP for review.

PCP review: nothing outstanding. Consistent with her history.

documents.title: Influenza vaccination
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Seasonal influenza vaccine, left deltoid, IM. Feeling well today, no prior reactions. VIS given. Tolerated; left after a short wait.

documents.title: Your June physical
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Ms. Kenney, with the pandemic restrictions we are pausing in-person preventive visits for now. We'll reach out to reschedule your physical for later this summer. If you need anything sooner, message or call us and the doctor can see you by video.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Masked visit. Has been working from home since spring and finds she sits more. Otherwise feels fine. Periods regular. No new symptoms. No medications.

Exam: comfortable. Heart regular without murmur, lungs clear, abdomen benign, no peripheral swelling. Vitals per flowsheet.

Plan: CBC with this year's labs. Flu vaccine in October. Co-test not due. Encouraged a daily walk now that her commute is gone. Return in a year.

documents.title: Blood count
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your blood count came back normal, no anemia.

documents.title: Flu shot
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Curbside screening done, afebrile, no symptoms. Quadrivalent flu vaccine given right deltoid. No issues.

documents.title: COVID-19 vaccination record
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Patient uploaded a photo of her vaccination card through the portal. Pfizer dose 1 on 04/09/2021 and dose 2 on 04/30/2021, both at a retail pharmacy. Entered into immunization history and state registry checked; matches.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
34F, well. Back in the office at work three days a week. Fully vaccinated for COVID in April. Periods monthly, about five days, no change. No meds, no allergies.

ROS negative. Exam: well. Normal heart and lung exam, abdomen soft and nontender, no edema. Vitals reviewed.

A/P: health maintenance. Basic labs. PHQ-2 0. Pap next due 2024. Flu in the fall. RTC one year.

documents.title: Labs from your physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: All of yesterday's results are in the normal range. Have a good summer.

documents.title: Influenza vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Came after work for her flu shot. No contraindications. Given IM left arm, lot logged. She'll get a COVID booster at her pharmacy when eligible.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit: Heavy Menses
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Since about July her periods have gotten longer and heavier. Now running well over a week, with big clots, and cramping bad enough that she has left work early twice. Using pads and tampons together on the heaviest days. Cycle still monthly. Not pregnant per her; not currently trying. No bleeding between periods or after intercourse. Mother had fibroids.
O: Looks well. Vitals per flowsheet. Abdomen soft, nontender, no palpable mass.
A: Heavy menstrual bleeding, likely structural given family history.
P: Gynecology referral placed for evaluation and pelvic imaging. She has an opening there in mid-January and would rather have blood drawn once, so the gyn office will check her counts at that visit. Call if she feels faint or soaks a pad an hour.

documents.title: Gyn appointment
documents.author: patient
documents.body: The gyn office called, I'm booked for January 17. Just letting you know.

documents.title: RE: Gyn appointment
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Thanks for the update, we sent your referral and notes over. Happy holidays.
